11:Silent data corruption (SDC) on a single physical core of a production ARM64 server (HiSilicon Kunpeng-920 / TaiShan V110) manifested as recurring kernel panics across five independent boots over twelve days, every event pinned to logical CPU 179. We perform a five-kdump forensic study combining (1) bit-exact register-vs-memory comparison at the crash instant, (2) ARMv8 architectural-invariant reasoning on `FAR_EL1`, and (3) microarchitectural modeling against community-documented TSV110 geometry (from `docs/cpu/kunpeng.md`, a community-maintained summary — not a vendor datasheet; HiSilicon does not publish a public TSV110 RTL/datasheet, so the geometric arguments are *conditional* on this geometry being correct — see §2.1). We identify signatures **consistent with** three specific microarchitectural data paths (Fig. 1; the mechanism is not independently silicon-verified — see §3.5/§7): **D1** — the core-private load data-return path (fill-buffer/replay-merge ≈ L1D readout mux); **D2** — the AGU→MMU address-presentation path; and **D3** — the page-table-walker (PTW) readout path. The decisive new evidence: a load of `__per_cpu_offset[146]` returned a value bit-identical to `__per_cpu_offset[0]` right-rotated by one byte — a structural byte-lane skew uniquely matching the array head among all 192 slots (Hamming distance 0; the XOR-distance from the stale-replay source `slot[0]` — the value the load actually returned, per the stale-replay model — to this signature is 30 bits, so no pure k<30-bit flip reproduces it; the XOR-distance from the *truth* `slot[146]` to the signature is 26 bits). This shows the conventional **bit-flip** fault model cannot reproduce the defect; a **structural** (byte-lane-skew) fault model is required.
113:- **D1 — Load data-return path (fill-buffer / replay-merge).** A load of `__per_cpu_offset[146]` returned `__per_cpu_offset[0]` (array head) byte-rotated by one byte (the 15:58 case, Hamming-0; the 08-14 case reaches only Hamming-6 and corroborates the head-slot preference). *Rotation direction is degenerate for a 64-bit word: `ror1(x) ≡ rol7(x)` (1+7=8 bytes = whole word), so 15:58 is identified under a (ror1, rol7) ambiguity — symmetric to the 08-14 (ror6, rol2) ambiguity; the load-bearing fact is the Hamming-0 rotation, not its direction.* This byte displacement has an XOR-distance of 30 bits from the stale-replay source (`slot[0]`, the value the load actually returned per the stale-replay model) — and 26 bits from the *truth* (`slot[146]`) — so it is **not expressible as any pure k<30-bit flip** (or k<26 from the truth); reproducing it required the structural `byte_lane_skew` model (§4.1), which end-to-end reproduces the chain skewed-pointer → non-canonical VA → page fault → Kernel Oops (H5, consistency-checked; §5.1).
191:- **Boot 15:58 (hard evidence):** `x20 = 0x00ffffcc879da2e0` matches `ror1(__per_cpu_offset[0])` (right-rotate by one byte) at Hamming distance 0 (the nearest other candidate is slot[3] at distance 2 — see the reproducibility-grading note below; this "nearest" figure requires the full 192-slot array, which lives only in the non-redistributable 180 GB vmcore). The load targeted slot 146. **Independently re-verified from the original 0102-board vmcore**: `crash` reads `__per_cpu_offset[0] = 0xffffcc879da2e000` (@ `0xffffb378e29e55d0`) and `__per_cpu_offset[146] = 0xffffcc879ed92000` (the truth the load should have returned); `ror1(slot[0]) = 0x00ffffcc879da2e0 == x20` (Hamming 0), and `Hamming(x20, slot[146]) = 26` (confirming x20 is corrupted, not the truth). *Rotation-direction degeneracy (symmetric to the 08-14 case): for a 64-bit word, `ror1(x) ≡ rol7(x)` (1+7=8 bytes = whole word), so `rol7(slot[0])` *also* matches x20 at Hamming-0; the 15:58 signature is therefore identified under a (ror1, rol7) ambiguity, exactly parallel to the 08-14 (ror6, rol2) ambiguity noted below. The load-bearing fact is the Hamming-0 byte-rotation match itself — which is unreachable by any bit-flip — not the *right*-rotation direction (either of ror1/rol7 reaches it with 0 bit flips).* *(An earlier draft wrote `rol1` here; that was a notation slip — but the slip also masks the deeper point that the direction is genuinely ambiguous, which we now disclose.)*
194:Two independent boots, two different rotation magnitudes (1 byte for 15:58; 6-or-2 bytes for 08-14 per the degeneracy above), both hitting the *array head* (slot 0 in both boots — the 08-14 boot's `__per_cpu_offset[0]` is `0xffffd93715b7e000`, a different value from 15:58's `0xffffcc879da2e000` because the per-cpu offset array differs across boots/KASLR, but the matched slot is index 0, the head, in both) — 15:58 at Hamming-0, 08-14 at Hamming-6. We do **not** over-claim a "random coincidence probability" here (a prior version cited ≈2⁻⁵⁸; we withdraw it as circular — the fill-buffer stale-replay model *predicts* that the corrupted value comes from the oldest fill-buffer entry, which is the array head first-touched at boot, so "matching the head" is model-consistent, not a coincidence to be excluded). The load-bearing D1 evidence is instead: (i) the Hamming-0 byte-rotation match of the 15:58 case (reproducible bit-exactly; the nearest non-head candidate is at distance 2), and (ii) the **bit-flip unreachability, now stated with an explicit exhaustive bound**. *Labeling caveat (honest):* `slot[0]` is the **stale-replay source** (the value the load actually returned, per the stale-replay model), **not "the truth"** — the load targeted `slot[146]`, so the *truth* is `slot[146]=0xffffcc879ed92000`. We report both XOR-distances: from the stale-replay source `slot[0]` to the observed `x20`: `slot[0] ^ x20 = 0xff00334b1a3f42e0`, popcount **30**; and from the *truth* `slot[146]` to `x20`: `slot[146] ^ x20`, popcount **26**. The relevant bound depends on which value a bit-flip fault model would operate on: under the stale-replay premise the load returned `slot[0]`, so a bit-flip on the returned value would need *exactly 30 bits*; if instead one supposes the fault bit-flipped the truth `slot[146]` in transit, the bound is 26. Either way (k<30 or k<26) no pure bit-flip model reproduces the signature, whereas a single structural byte-permutation (ror1) reaches it with *0 bit flips*. We retain 30 as the headline bound (it is the conservative — larger — of the two, and corresponds to the paper's own stale-replay model), and disclose 26 for completeness so a skeptic can see both. An exhaustive search over the single-byte bit-flip space (8 bytes × 256 masks) finds no match (confirming single-byte, ≤8-bit flips are insufficient); the XOR-distances of 30 (stale source) and 26 (truth) close the bound for any k-bit pure-flip model with k < 30 (resp. k < 26). The corruption is thus a structural byte-lane re-route, not a bit flip — this is the signature of a fill-buffer/load-queue stale-entry replayed with a wrong byte-lane phase.

在两次崩溃（08-14、08-24）中，架构地址的 MSB ≠ 0（`0xd9…`、`0x55…`），而内核打印的 `FAR` 却 MSB = 0（`0x00…`）。我们必须诚实指出：此 D2 证据**比先前版本声称的弱**：(1) **`FAR_EL1[63:60]` 对翻译错误是 UNKNOWN/RES0**（§2.2，ARMv8-A ARM DDI 0487 §D13.2.30）——仅 `FAR[51:0]`（至 [55:0]）架构保证，故高位 nibble 差异本身非架构证据。(2) **TBI1（EL1/内核 top-byte 剥离）未被静态启用**——objdump 0102 单板 vmlinux `__cpu_setup` 显示无 `TCR_EL1.TBI1`（bit 38）立即数；`CONFIG_ARM64_TAGGED_ADDR_ABI=y` 只动态启用 TBI0（EL0/用户）按进程。*（保留：此为对 `__cpu_setup` 初始化路径的静态分析；运行时 `mrs tcr_el1` 读取——经内核模块或 crash 的 per-cpu TCR——才是闭合裁决，且未执行。若后续运行时写 TCR_EL1 置 TBI1，该静态结论不会捕捉到。）* **然而，TBI 分析对这些案例*不适用*（对先前"部分恢复"框架的更正）**：TBI1 控制 MMU 是否对*有效*内核 VA 做 top-byte 剥离；但 0814/0824 的 `arch_addr` 高字节 0xd9/0x55 **非**有效内核地址——它们本身是 D1 坏值的非规范高字节（规范内核地址是 0xffff…）。故"TBI1-off 意味内核不对*有效*内核地址做剥离"这一结论，对这些*已损坏*地址的 MSB-vs-FAR 差异是缺陷还是损坏输入的伪迹，什么也没说明。TBI 在此既不 rescue 也不进一步损害 D2——该分析对被援引的两案例是 moot 的。(3) "arch MSB ≠ FAR MSB"观察因此被 D1 **混淆**（架构地址本身是 D1 坏值），独立于 TBI 点。**净结论：D2 从"已确认-弱"降级为"未证候选"（不再称"部分恢复"——TBI"部分恢复"对已损坏地址是非 sequitur）——地址通路机制在仿真可演练（§5.3），但硅证据被 D1 混淆（架构地址本身损坏），且 TBI 分析对所涉两案例不适用。** 完全裁决 D2 需一个架构地址是真正规范内核地址而 FAR 显示不同高字节的案例——5 转储中无此案例。
